name: write-four-shorts-no-signed-byte-could-hold
rationale: An owned fixture whose only output is a texture2d<short, access::write>, writing the four shorts -32768, -129, 128 and 32767 -- every one of them outside the signed byte range, so a storage image only eight bits wide could not carry any of them and would leave 0, 127, -128 and -1 instead. It is the corpus's first signed 16-bit texture and its first authored air.write_texture_2d.s.v4i16. Note that it does NOT discriminate the storage-image format the emitter declares: MoltenVK writes through the bound texture's own format, so this case matches whether the module declares Rgba8i or Rgba16i. What it pins is that the signed-short write path binds, dispatches and round-trips every representable short.

name: manual-float4-fetch-depth-zero-triangle

name: a14-nhwc-half-2x2-kernel-six-by-five-channels-two-images
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). Constant 89 = 0x56 states C mod 16 = 6 and O mod 16 = 5 and selects no linking, no reduction, not 1x1 and not the 16x16 multiply (bit 17 clear); constant 124 = 0x101b607 selects unit stride, unit dilation, one group, NHWC (bit 26 clear), tiles O = C = K = 8, one k-split and one simdgroup per threadgroup, both tiles in registers (no threadgroup staging), the image edge check, and C and O not multiples of their tiles. So the entry takes the A14 NHWC kernel, which multiplies half 8x8 simdgroup matrices into float accumulators, each lane building its two fragment cells from its lane index (the device-measured layout: row ((L >> 1) & 3) | ((L >> 4) << 2), columns ((L >> 3) & 1) 4 + (L & 1) 2 and the next). The 448-byte parameters (binding 26): 6 input and 5 output channels, a 2 x 2 kernel, batch 2 in one sub-batch, a 5 x 2 source and a 5 x 2 gradient, offsets (-1, 0), 10 gradient positions per image (one full 8-position chunk and a 2-position tail), 16-bit magic divisors 2 (kW, kH) and 5 (gradient width) and the 32-bit divisor 5, uber tiles 1, per-image element counts 50 and 60, weightsOutputChannels 5, numWeights 120. Four threadgroups of 32 threads, threadgroup x = ky 2 + kx, each compute dW[ky][kx][c][o] = sum over n, gy, gx of gradient[n][gy][gx][o] source[n][gy + ky][gx + kx - 1][c], loading zero for positions left of the source, channels past 6 and output channels past 5, and store it to destination word ((ky 2 + kx) 6 + c) 5 + o (HWIO; binding 27, poisoned 0xab, all 120 words written). Every source and gradient value is one of [-3.5, -3.0, -2.5, -2.0, -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0], exact in half (exponents where both 8-bit conventions agree): source element i takes entry (7i + 3) mod 16, gradient element i entry (3i + 5) mod 16. Every product is a multiple of 1/4 of magnitude at most 25 and every sum (at most 20 terms) lies in [-35.75, 51.0], so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Loops are bounded by the two images, the two chunks per image and the fixed tile counts.

name: float-products-flushed-before-rounding-under-fast-math
rationale: Whether Metal flushes a float product whose exact value lies below 2^-126 but rounds to 2^-126 (tininess before rounding), under the default fast math, in vector and scalar multiplies and in dot's fused chain. Thread t reads the float4 operands a = in[2t] and b = in[2t + 1] and writes three float4 rows: a * b as one vector multiply; the same four products as scalar multiplies of scalar loads; and dot(a, b), dot(a.xy, b.xy), dot(a.zw, b.zw) and dot(a.yzw, b.yzw). 256 lanes: 10 hand lanes (an exact product of 2^-126 (1 - 2^-24), exactly 2^-126, just above it, the representable 2^-126 - 2^-149, and a product just below 2^-126 from operands above and below 1, each with both signs), 230 random lanes whose significand product lies within two units of 2^47 or 2^48 with exponent sums placing it next to 2^-126, both signs, and 16 ordinary products. Metal answers the zero of the sign on 36 product lanes where a device that rounds first and keeps denormals answers 2^-126, 16 of them (exact products in [2^-126 (1 - 2^-25), 2^-126)) where one that flushes after its rounding does too; 56 of the 256 dots differ between a chain that flushes before rounding and one that rounds first. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: nan-model-float-denormals-per-operation-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_denormals_fast (nan_denormals' program under the default fast math: the calls are the fast_ ones and the arithmetic carries every flag; the flagged state of class J, DESIGN D293). Lane i reads (a, b, c) and writes 48 words: a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b, fma(a, b, c), a * b + c, -a, 0 - a, fabs(a), copysign(a, b), a < b and a == b as 0 or 1; floor, ceil, trunc, round, rint, fract, sign, saturate, sqrt, rsqrt, log2, log, sin, tan, atan, asin, sinh, tanh, asinh, atanh of a; pow(a, b), powr(a, b), fmod(a, b), ldexp(a, 4), dot(float2(a, b), float2(b, c)), length(float2(a, b)), mix(a, b, c), step(a, b), smoothstep(a, b, c), atan2(a, b), fmin(a, b), (a * b) * c, (a / b) * c, a < b ? a : b, -(a * b), and fabs(a - b). Lanes: every pair (a, b) of +-2^-149, 3 * 2^-149, 2^-127, both largest denormals, +-2^-126, +-1, 0.5, 3, 2^-100, 2^-30, 2^-120, and 2^10, with c from the same set: denormal operands of each sign, and normal pairs whose product, quotient, or difference is a denormal. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: mark-every-nonzero-signed-channel-of-a-two-by-two
rationale: Each of the four threads fetches its own signed texel, takes the componentwise absolute value and writes one where that magnitude is positive. name: resolve-a-bilinear-tap-from-a-gathered-array-footprint
rationale:
ksShadowOcclusionDownsampleSUDepthArray resolves one bilinear tap by hand: it gathers the four texels of the footprint with `air.gather_texture_2d_array.v4f16`, builds the four bilinear weights from the fractional part of the same coordinate, normalizes them by their own sum, and dots the two together -- once per array layer, walking the layer count the output texture reports. It reaches the coordinate through `air.convert.f.v2f16.u.v2i16` on the thread position assembled from `threadgroup_position_in_grid * threads_per_threadgroup + thread_position_in_threadgroup`.

The weights and the gather order have to agree, and this case is what says they do. The shader lays its four weights out as fy(1-fx), fx*fy, fx(1-fy), (1-fx)(1-fy); Metal's gather returns the footprint as (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0) from a base of floor(coord*extent - 0.5). Pairing them any other way would weight the wrong corner. The first and third weights are equal here, so the case cannot separate those two taps -- that is a property of the shader, not of the authoring -- but the second and fourth differ from them and from each other, so the diagonal pair is pinned.

Both textures are four by four so the coordinate maps one thread to one texel, and four is a power of two so the reciprocals the shader takes of the output extent are exact halves. The shader offsets by -0.498046875 rather than -0.5, and `fract` of an integer minus that is 0.501953125 whichever integer it is, negative or not -- so all sixteen threads share one weight vector, 257/512 and 255/512. Those are exact in binary32, their four products are exact, and the products sum to exactly one, so the normalizing divide is a divide by one and cannot round. Truncated to half the weights are 0.25, 0.251953125, 0.25 and 0.248046875 -- 128, 129, 128 and 127 over 512.

Every texel is an integer below four, so each dot product is (128a + 129b + 128c + 127d)/512 with a numerator below 2048: exact in binary16, and so is every partial sum, which is what makes the association the fast-math flags choose irrelevant. Twelve of the sixteen threads have a tap at column or row -1 and exercise the sampler's clamp to edge. The two layers carry different tables, so the loop over the output's array size has to advance the gather's layer operand with it.

This case holds no non-finite texel, so the four bit tests the shader runs on the gathered halves -- masking off the sign and comparing against the exponent-all-ones pattern -- all answer false and every tap reaches the dot product unchanged.

name: substitute-a-constant-for-a-gathered-quiet-nan
rationale:

This case makes one texel of layer 0 a quiet NaN, 0x7e00. The shader tests each gathered half by masking off its sign bit and comparing the result against 0x7c00 as an unsigned integer, so infinities pass and only NaNs fail, and a failing lane is replaced with the literal 5.0 before the dot. Four threads gather that texel, each into a different lane of the footprint, so the substitution is observed once per lane and at three different weights. The test is an integer comparison on the bit pattern rather than a floating-point predicate, which is why the module's `no-nans-fp-math` does not make it dead.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat-64-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (offset 0, 256 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[k][n] (row stride w_ld = 64 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in bfloat and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the bfloat inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat-64-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed counterpart of the committed qmm_t_64_bfloat case (DESIGN D272): qmm_n_64_bfloat with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links three translation units, each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: linked-k24-gather-qvm-n-bfloat
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry (DESIGN D296), whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select N = 32 outputs (one threadgroup's 32 columns) over K = 24 rows: the guard (threadgroup_position.y << 5) < N passes, lanes 0 to 23 each dequantize one 8-bit row of W (row stride N bytes) and scale it, the simdgroup sums the 32 partial results, and lane 0 hands all 32 to the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at element indices 0 to 31 (128 bytes, observed whole). x holds 1, 2, 3 repeating, the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-qvm-n-bfloat
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A single invocation and unit gather batch select literal index zero from the authored buffers. The quantized K extent and vector-row count are zero while the quantization group size is one, making every accumulation and final postfix loop zero-trip and leaving the sole bounded destination element unchanged. name: splat-one-motion-vector-over-four-seeded-texels
rationale: A zero content scale keeps the splat footprint on the thread's own texel, so the single invocation issues all ten texture maxes at known coordinates and no two threads can race. The motion vector packs to the half bits of one and three, and a depth of exactly one supplies the high word, so the splatted word is known and the four seeded texels sit at, below, above and far above it -- the maxes therefore win twice, lose once, and leave the saturated texel alone. The thread's own texel also receives the second, unset-high-bit spelling of the same word, which is smaller, so it proves the operation is a maximum and not a store.

name: constant-buffer-float4-to-mrt2-highest
rationale: The loop-free fragment converts the exact finite float4 color in the 32-byte constant buffer to half4 and structurally inserts that same value into both return members; selecting attachment one verifies the complete two-target aggregate mapping.

name: zero-three-memset-lengths-that-do-not-match-their-object
rationale: Three llvm.memset calls whose LENGTH does not equal the object the destination pointer names, which is the whole difficulty of lowering memset without a byte address. Box is float2 + float + float. Clearing 4 of a Box's 16 bytes cuts through the float2, so emit_typed_zero_prefix (18 corpus sources, previously with no authored case) has to recurse into the vector and null only lane 0; clearing 12 bytes stores a whole null float2 and a null float and leaves f2 alone. The third clears sixteen bytes through a pointer to a SINGLE device float -- out + 8 -- which is the run the emitter used to answer with one store, silently leaving out[9..11] at their initial 0xAB pattern. Buffer 0 is (1, 2, 3, 4) so every surviving member is a distinct exact binary32 integer and every cleared one is zero: the answer is (0, 2, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0). Clearing one lane too many writes 0 at slot 1; one too few writes 1 at slot 0 or 3 at slot 6; the short element run leaves 0xABABABAB in slots 9 through 11. The AIR is hand-written because the smallest corpus host for the over-long run is rwppRigidSolver at 908 lines, and no Metal source can spell a memset that outruns its pointee -- the frontend only produces one from an array element pointer, which is what the AIR does directly.

name: division-flags-and-fast-sincos-under-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): how Metal divides under each fast-math flag set, compiled with the default fast math, and whether fast::sincos flushes past the last quadrant as fast::sin and fast::cos do. Each of 512 threads writes 16 words: x / y and 1 / y with every fast flag, without reassoc (reassociate off), and without contract (contract off), fast::divide(x, y) and (1, y) (reassoc nsz arcp contract afn), precise::divide(x, y) and (1, y) (no flag), x / y and z / y dividing by one load of y, fast::sincos(t)'s sine and cosine, and fast::sin(t) and fast::cos(t). Every other quotient divides by its own load of y (all copies hold the same value), so no division shares its divisor and each reciprocal word is Metal's 1 / y beside its quotient. Operands (x, y): 160 generic quotients with exponents in [-20, 20]; 48 divisors about 2^126 (2^126 itself, its neighbours, 2^127, the largest float, values just below) with numerators whose correctly rounded quotient is a normal number; 48 quotients in or near the float denormals; 32 denormal divisors; 32 divisors about 2^-126; 32 pairs of zeros, infinities, NaN, and finite values; 32 quotients past or near the largest float; 32 powers of two and equal operands; the rest over the whole exponent range. z is a generic numerator. The angles t: 160 in [-2^-8, 4), 64 up to 2^22, 64 within 16 half-ulps of float(pi/2) * 2^22 = 6588397.5 of either sign, 96 past it up to the largest float, 16 special values (signed zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals, 2^-126, the largest float, the limit and its neighbour), and the rest in [-2^24, 2^24]. The AIR has no loop.
